# 0071: A cell is judged by its Important Metrics, each reduced over the cell's samples by its own aggregates

Status: accepted, 2026-10-17.
Supersedes part 3 of [0042](0042-the-overview-is-filtered-by-the-url.md): the summary no longer aggregates every measure by one arithmetic mean.
Extends [0021](0021-metric-names-carry-unit-and-provenance.md) (a metric name carries its unit and its source) and [0037](0037-the-emitted-records-are-types-and-the-cache-tree-has-one-owner.md) (the emitted records are types).
Extends [0065](0065-a-subagent-is-priced-at-its-own-models-rates.md), whose per-subagent estimate the cost share divides.

## Context

The treatment-axis sweeps ran the same cell twice and got two different verdicts.
One run per cell cannot separate a treatment's effect from noise, so a cell has to be run more than once.
Each run already records its own session, so nothing in the runner needed to change to take repeated samples.

What was missing was a way to judge a cell across them.
The overview summary led with a pass count and averaged every other measure by one arithmetic mean (ADR 0042, part 3).
A mean of a heavy-tailed cost lets one runaway session drag the whole row.
Several measures a skill is judged by were not recorded per cell at all: subagent delegation, compactions, and the share of output spent on reasoning.

## Decision

**The Important Metrics are declared once.** `IMPORTANT_METRICS` in `model/metrics.py` names each metric, the history field it reads, an optional denominator, its kind and its unit.
`emit/` aggregates that list, the report renders its columns from it, and the glossary names it, so adding a metric is one edit.

**A sample is one graded session of a cell.** A cell is one skill, case, harness, model, effort and treatment.
A session whose verdict is `pass`, `fail` or `error` is a sample of its cell.
A dry run, or a record whose verdict this version cannot read, is not a sample.

**Each metric's kind fixes its aggregates.** A spread (cost, tokens, turns, throughput, wall clock) reduces to its median and quartiles.
A fraction (a share of a whole, a percentage of the window) reduces to its mean, minimum and maximum.
A rare count (subagents, compactions) reduces to its mean and the share of samples where it happened at all.
The verdict reduces to a pass rate with its Wilson 95% interval, which is honest at every sample size.
Every kind also reports `n`, the samples that recorded the metric.
A sample that did not record it drops out of `n` and is never counted as zero.

**Python reduces, the page renders.** `emit/samples.py` groups every stored history line into its cell and writes the result into `index.json` as `important_metrics`.
The page looks each cell's aggregates up by its group key and computes none.
Every overview filter is part of that key or a property of the model, so a filter drops whole cells and never splits one.

**The missing per-cell fields are recorded for both harnesses.** `compactions` counts the records of a new `compaction` category.
Those are Claude's `compact_boundary` system record and Codex's `compacted` record.
`reasoning_share` divides reasoning by output tokens.
Claude reports its thinking tokens, and both providers bill reasoning inside output.
`subagents`, `subagent_token_share` and `subagent_cost_share` measure delegation.
`output_tokens_per_sec_by_model` splits throughput by the model that answered each call.

**The report leads with the Important Metrics.** The overview's first table is one row per cell, each metric showing its headline aggregate and every aggregate on its title.
The verdict is one column among them, never the first thing read.

## Consequences

Running a cell several times now pays off.
Its row reports a median, a spread and a pass rate with an interval, rather than one run's word.
A record written before these fields existed stays readable and shows as not recorded, never as a cell that never delegated or compacted.

The overview table is wider than one screen at common widths, so its scroll box becomes a tab stop.
The table that budgets its width to one screen remains the sessions table (ADR 0043).

The page no longer averages anything itself, so a measure the summary shows and the number in `index.json` cannot disagree.
A future self-evaluation loop can read the same document.

## Lens

Pass or fail is one signal among many, and one run is one sample.
Judge a cell by everything it measured, across every time it ran.
Reduce each measure the way its distribution deserves, and say how many samples the number stands on.
